question: What will the first reported revenues after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Apple)

calls.reasoning: Apple guided Sept-quarter FY26 revenue +9-11% y/y on Q4 FY25's $102.47B (~$111.7-113.7B). Recent record vs guidance midpoint: Q4FY25 -1pp, Q1FY26 +5pp, Q2FY26 about +2.5pp, Q3FY26 about +0.5pp (16.3% vs 14-17%). Consensus is ~$113.4-115.3B. Downside: heavy supply constraints (advanced nodes, memory), a 2.5pp FX headwind, and Sept-Oct reports of soft iPhone 18 Pro demand and 15-20% order cuts, which mostly hit October. Upside: big iPhone 18 Pro price increases lift ASP, plus strong Services (+12-16%). Median ~$113.6B. Below-$112B tail ~17% (a low-end miss like Q4FY25); above $118B ~3%. No human prediction market found on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold.

Resolves off Apple's reported total revenue in its earnings release, not on segment figures or analyst estimates.
- Event window: quarter ended late Sept 2026 (100% elapsed as of 2026-10-11). Only the report itself is still pending, on Nov 2, 2026, which is after the listed Oct 29 resolution timestamp.
- Base: Q4 FY25 revenue was $102.47B.
- Guidance (Jul 30, 2026 call): total revenue +9-11% y/y (≈$111.7-113.7B). FX is a ~2.5pp sequential headwind. Supply constraints are expected to hurt iPhone, Mac and iPad 'significantly' (advanced-node chip availability, memory costs). iPhone is guided to grow mid-teens y/y. Gross margin 47-48%; opex $19.1-19.4B (MacRumors Jul 30 2026).
- Recent actuals vs guidance: Q3 FY26 (June quarter) $109.4B, +16%, vs a 14-17% guide. Q2 FY26 (March quarter) $111.2B, +17%, vs consensus ~$108.9B. Q1 FY26 +16% vs a ~10-12% guide. Q4 FY25 +8% vs an 8-10% guide (low end).
- Q3 FY26 segments: iPhone $54.3B (+22%), Mac $10.4B (+29%), Services $30.7B (+12%).
- Analyst consensus for Q4 FY26 revenue differs by source: ~$113.4B (MarketBeat), ~$114.3B, ~$115.3B (Oct 2026 aggregators).
- Sept 15 2026 (Invezz): AAPL fell as analysts weighed iPhone 18 Pro and foldable demand; early lead times are running below last year (JPMorgan); UBS flags demand-elasticity risk from price hikes.
- Oct 9 2026 (MacRumors/AppleInsider): reports say Apple cut iPhone 18 Pro component orders for October by 15-20% after a price hike. These cuts mainly affect the Dec quarter, not Sept.
- iPhone 18 Pro prices reportedly up $250-300 (Jeff Pu), which raises ASP.
- Launch quarter includes iPhone 18 Pro launch weeks, Watch Series 12, Watch Ultra 4 and AirPods 5.
- Prediction markets: searched Polymarket, Kalshi and Manifold; found no Apple-revenue contract.
- Could not find: post-quarter channel checks quantifying September iPhone sell-in, or any Apple pre-announcement.

calls.reconciliation: Factual: all runs agree on base ($102.47B), guide (+9-11%), Nov 2 report date, prior-quarter actuals, and that no prediction market exists; the consensus spread ($113.4-115.3B) reflects aggregator differences and cannot be settled without web access. Judgment: the below-$112B tail (Run 1 17% vs Runs 2-3 7-8%). Apple usually lands at or above its guide midpoint, and the only recent low-end landing (FQ4'25) still beat the bottom of its range; supply-constrained quarters tend to sell everything built. The Oct order cuts concern the Dec quarter. I put the tail at ~10%, the median slightly above the top of the guide, and accept Runs 2-3's dispersion logic, slightly widened.
